english.title: Racially / religiously aggravated harassment with fear of violence
english.standardoffencewording:

(A)_[him]_
(B)_[her]_

by your course of conduct, which you knew or ought to have known would cause fear of violence to

(C)_[him,]_
(D)_[her,]_

in that **(..SPECIFY THE DATES IF DIFFERENT FROM ABOVE, LOCATIONS AND NATURE OF CONDUCT..) and the offence was

english.legislation: Contrary to section 32(1)(b) and (4) of the Crime and Disorder Act 1998.

english.notes:
(i) The maximum penalty on indictment was increased from seven to 14 years from 3rd April 2017, see H18819/CD98076 for offences committed on or after that date. That offence also applies where the conduct occurred over two or more days before and after that date, see section 175 of the Policing and Crime Act 2017.
(ii) The option to return an alternative verdict of guilty of the basic offence is not available in the magistrates court, therefore the basic offence should be charged in addition to the aggravated offence.
(iii) Harassing a person may include alarming or causing the person distress; a "course of conduct" must involve conduct on at least two occasions and "conduct" includes speech.
(iv) The conduct must have taken place on at least two occasions on or after 30 September 1998.
(v) If, on trial on indictment of a person charged with this offence, the jury find him not guilty of the offence charged, they may find him guilty of the offence of racially aggravated harassment under section 2 of the Protection from Harassment Act 1997 and section 32(6) of the Crime and Disorder Act 1998.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Seven years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
